AnalyseRequest.description:
Analysis inputs.

Costs, price and volume are supplied by the caller rather than invented.  Each
carries its own provenance, and §13 refuses to compute a margin from a figure
whose origin is unstated.
AnalyseRequest.title: AnalyseRequest

AnalyzeRequest.description: Untrusted external content to analyse as data (§12.4, §20 G).
AnalyzeRequest.title: AnalyzeRequest

AutonomyRequest.description: Levels 3 and 4 are excluded by the Literal, so they cannot be requested.
AutonomyRequest.title: AutonomyRequest

BudgetBand.description:
Startup-capital bands (§7).  ``CUSTOM`` covers any owner-stated figure
that does not fall in a preset band.
BudgetBand.title: BudgetBand

BudgetConstraint.description:
The owner's stated capital limit.

§13 forbids the engine from silently raising this figure.  It is therefore
immutable in practice: ``available_capital`` is captured once, with the
currency and the fact of whether the owner actually stated it.  Any
downstream analysis that needs more money must return
``INCOMPATIBLE`` - it may not amend this record.
BudgetConstraint.title: BudgetConstraint

BusinessCategory.description: The seven categories an opportunity may belong to (§6).
BusinessCategory.title: BusinessCategory

CostItem.description:
One cost line.  ``provenance`` is mandatory and ``UNKNOWN`` never means
zero - it means the analysis cannot price this line.
CostItem.title: CostItem

DiscoverRequest.description:
Inputs for candidate generation (§7).

Every field is optional.  A request carrying nothing but a budget still
produces budget-driven candidates, and the five evidence-dependent methods
report that they produced nothing rather than inventing demand.
DiscoverRequest.title: DiscoverRequest

DiscoveryMethod.description:
The six ways a candidate may be produced (§7).

A method describes *how the candidate was derived*, which is what makes the
derivation auditable.  It is not a quality judgement: a budget-driven
candidate is not worse than a demand-driven one, it merely has a different
evidential starting point.
DiscoveryMethod.title: DiscoveryMethod

EmergencyRequest.description:
Reason is mandatory so the audit trail records why the owner acted.

Bounded length because it is persisted and echoed back to authorized
callers; it is never written to logs (see core/emergency.py).
EmergencyRequest.title: EmergencyRequest

EnqueueResearchRequest.description:
Submit a research sweep to the P-01 task manager (§24).

This enqueues work that the owner has asked for now.  It does not schedule
anything: deciding *when* to research autonomously is P-12, and the engine
reports ``autonomous_scheduling: false`` rather than implying a capability it
does not have.
EnqueueResearchRequest.title: EnqueueResearchRequest

OpportunityCandidate.description: A freshly discovered candidate, before any research (§7).
OpportunityCandidate.title: OpportunityCandidate

OpportunityState.description:
The opportunity lifecycle (§17).

The first eight are the forward path; the rest are non-forward outcomes.
Note that ``NEEDS_MORE_EVIDENCE`` is a *live* state with a way back into
research, while ``REJECTED``, ``INCOMPATIBLE`` and ``BLOCKED_BY_COMPLIANCE``
are terminal for the purposes of recommendation.
OpportunityState.title: OpportunityState

Provenance.description:
How a numeric figure came to be (§13).

``UNKNOWN`` is mandatory rather than optional: the commercial model refuses
to treat a missing figure as zero.
Provenance.title: Provenance

ReasonRequest.description: A reason is mandatory for every state change, so the audit trail explains itself.
ReasonRequest.title: ReasonRequest

SourceRegisterRequest.description:
A source declaration (§8).

No credential field exists here.  Authentication is declared by mechanism; the
secret is never accepted, stored or returned.
SourceRegisterRequest.title: SourceRegisterRequest

post.description: Analyse untrusted external content as data, never as instructions.

Change the autonomy level. Owner-only by permission (§15).

`authorized_by_owner` is established here by the permission check having
passed for `intelligence.autonomy`, which only the owner holds. It is never
taken from the request body — a model or an agent could otherwise assert it.
Submit an owner message and receive a structured intelligence response.

get.description: List the caller's missions, paginated and optionally filtered by state.

post.description: Interpret a request and, if it warrants one, create a mission.

Owner approval of a plan.

Approval authorizes execution *if the autonomy level permits it*. At the
default advisory level nothing is dispatched, and the response says so
plainly rather than implying the work has started (§15, §16).
Generate a plan for review. Launches nothing (§20 B).

get.description: Progress derived from real task states, never narrated by a model (§11.4).

post.description: Revise a plan, preserving the previous version and the reason (§9.6).

get.description:
Registered models and their health.

The `configuration` field is deliberately omitted: it is where a provider
base URL or credential would live, and §14 forbids exposing provider
configuration through API responses.

The nine-section report (§23).

``is_test_data`` defaults to true.  Asserting otherwise is an explicit claim
that every figure came from a real authorized source, and the schema refuses a
report that makes that claim while a test-data notice is still present.

A sweep that reaches no source still completes: it reports one refusal per
source attempted.  That is the finding, not a failure to hide.
